entry.title: 9 Tips to Make Antigravity CLI Less Painful
entry.content:
本文转载自 X 博主 @lemomo_ai（Lemomo） 的长文，原文链接，版权归原作者所有。

Gemini 4 is a strong model, but Google’s Antigravity is painful to use. Because most developers prefer connecting to a CLI when working remotely, this post focuses on the Antigravity CLI (abbreviated as agy) and shares a few settings that cut down the friction and make it less painful to use.

In daily terminal work, four pain points stand out:

  • Permission prompts pop up constantly: Cross-folder reads, scratch-file writes, MCP tool calls, and global skills installed through npx skills trigger repeated approval dialogs.
  • The context window size is fixed: Antigravity provides no setting to resize or tune the context window limit for your workload.
  • Context compaction is poor: Once a long session hits the compaction threshold, automatic summarization drops important details and degrades follow-up turns.
  • Input box shortcuts break terminal muscle memory: In agy, unlike Claude Code or Codex, pressing Esc once or Ctrl+C does not clear typed text in the prompt box, and pressing Esc twice (Esc Esc) does not rewind the conversation.

You cannot fix the fixed context window or the poor compaction until Google updates the harness itself. To make agy less painful today, here are nine practical fixes across three areas: taming permission prompts, customizing the UI, observability, and privacy, and adapting to its keyboard shortcuts.

Know Where Antigravity CLI Stores Its Config

Antigravity’s CLI (agy) and its GUI surfaces do not share the same configuration files or setup methods, because they have different architectures and feature sets—for example, the GUI supports rich visual capabilities such as Generative UI, whereas agy is a standalone, lightweight Go binary built for terminal and remote SSH workflows.

Important: Any permission preset or preference you change in a graphical Antigravity client will not apply to agy. The CLI reads and writes its own configuration files in ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/.

  • | CLI Configuration Item | Path in Antigravity CLI (agy) | Interactive Slash Command |

  • | :— | :— | :— |

  • | Runtime Settings & Tool Permissions | ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json | /settings (or /config) and /permissions |

  • | Custom Keybindings | ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/keybindings.json | /keybindings |

  • | Global Skills Directory | ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/skills/ (also scans ~/.gemini/skills/) | — |

  • All CLI settings and the permission allowlist live in ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json: You can edit this JSON file directly on disk, or update it live inside agy using /settings (for Agent Mode, Sandbox Mode, Non-Workspace Access, and Tool Permission) and /permissions (for the permission allowlist).

  • Global skills for agy live in ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/skills/: Skills placed outside this directory (and outside ~/.gemini/skills/) are either missed at startup or treated as external file accesses.

Tame Repetitive Permission Prompts

At first glance, Antigravity feels frustrating because its default settings prompt on nearly every action. Once you examine how its controls fit together, however, Antigravity’s permission model is built around three core concepts—Project, Workspace, and Sandbox:

  • Project: Groups one or more physical repository directories on disk under a single project (configured in agy via /projects or –add-dir, defaulting to the launch directory alone under default-cli-project).
  • Workspace: Formed by all directories configured in the active Project. When Agent Mode is set to Auto, Antigravity treats the Workspace as the sole default scope for file operations and intercepts even read_file calls outside it.
  • Sandbox: Builds an OS-level isolation boundary around the Workspace (configured in agy via “enableTerminalSandbox”: true, using Apple Seatbelt sandbox-exec on macOS and bwrap namespaces on Linux), letting you set Tool Permission to either auto-approve inside the sandbox and ask outside (“proceed-in-sandbox”) or auto-approve everywhere (“always-proceed”).

Once you see how Project, Workspace, and Sandbox relate (shown below), it becomes clear why the default settings stall constantly and how to configure auto-approval for different trust boundaries:

In the default state (shown below), even with Agent Mode set to Auto, agy runs with Sandbox Mode off, a single-folder default Project, Tool Permission set to Request review, and an empty permissions.allow list—so sibling repository accesses, shell commands, /private/tmp scratch files, system SDK reads, and MCP calls pause repeatedly for manual approval:

Before presenting the two complete auto-approval recipes, we need two building blocks: adding related repositories into the Workspace by configuring a Project, and populating the permission allowlist in the configuration file for common external accesses.

Add Other Repository Directories to the Workspace via Project

Because Antigravity’s default rule for read_file is Ask (Allowed in workspace)—auto-allowed inside the Workspace, but prompting outside it even when Non-Workspace Access is on—the cleanest way to stop read prompts across related repositories (such as a frontend repo, a backend repo, and shared specs) is to add those directories to the Workspace and Sandbox boundary by configuring a Project.

In agy, use /projects (or –project) to configure directories under a Project, or mount extra folders into the current Workspace with –add-dir and /add-dir:

  • Create and switch Projects immediately after entering agy: Switching Projects in agy always starts a new conversation. If you start chatting first and switch Projects mid-task, your current conversation stays behind in the old Project.
  • Remember to switch to the Project after creating it: Creating a new Project in agy does not activate it automatically. Until you explicitly select Switch to project (or launch with agy –project=), the session keeps running under the default default-cli-project and cross-folder reads continue to prompt.
  • Directories configured under the active Project are included in the Workspace: Every folder in the active Project gets automatic access for read_file, write_file, and sandboxed shell commands without prompting.

Populate the Permission Allowlist in Settings

For operations that sit outside your Project repository directories and would otherwise trigger Ask prompts—MCP servers, temporary file accesses under /private/tmp on macOS, and read access to system SDK directories (such as Apple’s SDK directories) or shared reference directories—populate the allow permission allowlist via /permissions or directly under “permissions” in ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json (evaluated in Deny > Ask > Allow order):

  • Category 1 — mcp(/) approves all tools on trusted MCP servers at once: In Antigravity’s permissions table, MCP calls default to Ask. Adding wildcards for your regular MCP servers—such as mcp(playwright/), mcp(chrome-devtools/), mcp(cua/) (Computer-Use Agent), mcp(github/), or mcp(context7/)—lets the agent call every tool on those servers without pausing.
  • Category 2 — write_file(/private/tmp) silences both read and write prompts under /private/tmp on macOS: On macOS, /tmp is a symbolic link to /private/tmp. When a tool resolves the real path /private/tmp/…, Antigravity treats it as outside the Workspace and prompts. Per the official permissions documentation, allowing write_file(/private/tmp) implicitly grants read_file(/private/tmp) as well, so one rule stops both read and write prompts for /private/tmp.
  • Category 3 — read_file(…) grants read access to system SDK directories (such as Apple’s SDK paths) and shared reference directories: Because paths outside the Workspace default to Ask, inspecting system headers or framework definitions (such as /Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/SDKs/ and /Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer/Platforms/ on macOS) or shared reference directories triggers a permission prompt. Adding these system SDK directories and reference folders to read_file(…) overrides “allowNonWorkspaceAccess”: false to stop repeat read prompts across every project and mounts those paths as read-only inside the terminal Sandbox.

Choose an Auto-Approval Recipe in Settings

With your Project directories and permissions.allow list in place, open /settings in agy (or edit ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json) and choose between two complete permission recipes based on whether you want a strict boundary check or unrestricted execution:

Recipe 1: Auto-Allow Inside the Sandbox Boundary

This recipe lets the agent run without prompts inside your Workspace (including repositories added to your Project), terminal Sandbox, and permissions.allow paths, while pausing for confirmation whenever it tries to read or write an external path that you have not added to the Project or allowlist (shown below).

Launch agy with your multi-directory Project (or mount sibling directories on the fly):

And place the complete permission and allowlist configuration in ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json:

Recipe 2: Always Proceed Everywhere

If you work in a dedicated cloud VM or container—or simply want the agent to charge ahead across both Workspace and external directories without stopping for file permission prompts—set “toolPermission” to “always-proceed” and “allowNonWorkspaceAccess” to true. Because external file reads, writes, /private/tmp, and SDK directories are approved automatically, you do not need to configure a multi-directory Project or file-path allowlist rules; only the trusted MCP server rules remain in permissions.allow (or launch with agy –dangerously-skip-permissions to skip even MCP prompts, as shown below):

Here is how the core settings in both recipes interact:

  • Keep Agent Mode (“agentMode”) set to “auto”: Although Agent Mode offers Default, Plan, Auto, and Accept Edits (cycled with Shift + Tab), “auto” is the standard choice for daily work and approves file reads and writes inside your current Workspace (note that Antigravity’s permission rules only define read_file and write_file—there is no separate edit_file permission action).
  • Turn on Sandbox Mode (“enableTerminalSandbox”: true): By default, agy runs outside the Sandbox. Enabling Sandbox Mode isolates terminal commands using Apple Seatbelt (sandbox-exec) on macOS or bwrap namespaces on Linux, blocking unauthorized network access and host secrets (such as ~/.ssh) while unlocking Proceed in sandbox.
  • Under Recipe 1, keep Non-Workspace Access (“allowNonWorkspaceAccess”) set to false to avoid the “prompts on reads, silent on writes” trap: When “allowNonWorkspaceAccess” is false, any access outside the Workspace pops up a three-option menu whose second option permanently enables Non-Workspace Access. Many users select that second option hoping to stop repeat prompts, which triggers a counterintuitive trap in Auto mode: because Auto mode auto-approves file edits while read_file falls back to Ask (Allowed in workspace), flipping “allowNonWorkspaceAccess” to true under “proceed-in-sandbox” causes Antigravity to still prompt when reading an unwhitelisted external file, yet silently create or overwrite any file outside your Workspace (write_file) without a single prompt! Conversely, permissions.allow rules take precedence over “allowNonWorkspaceAccess”: false: in Recipe 1, keeping “allowNonWorkspaceAccess” set to false and adding your trusted external paths to permissions.allow lets those whitelisted paths pass with zero prompts while blocking both unwhitelisted external reads and unwhitelisted external writes.
  • Set Tool Permission (“toolPermission”) to select your recipe: The default Request review setting prompts before every git status, npm test, or ls -la. Switching to “proceed-in-sandbox” (Recipe 1) auto-approves everything inside the Workspace, Sandbox, and permissions.allow list while prompting outside it; switching to “always-proceed” (Recipe 2) auto-approves file reads, writes, and commands both inside and outside the Workspace.

Fix Permission Prompts Caused by the Wrong npx skills Install Directory

Global skills installed with npx skills fail to load at startup and trigger permission prompts when read because npx skills installs them into the wrong directory. Running npx skills add <owner/repo> -g places skill files in /.agents/skills/ instead of agy’s actual global skills directory (/.gemini/antigravity-cli/skills/). Because ~/.agents/skills/ sits outside agy’s skills directory and outside your active Workspace, reading a skill’s SKILL.md or helper scripts triggers an external file access prompt.

Fix this by linking ~/.agents/skills back to ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/skills/ with a symbolic link (ln -s, or a macOS Finder alias):

  • Subsequent npx skills installs land in the right directory: Every npx skills add <owner/repo> -g command now writes straight into ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/skills/, so agy discovers your skills at startup and reads them without prompting.

Customize the UI, Observability, and Privacy

By default, agy collects usage telemetry, exposes your personal account information in the top bar, cycles through usage tips at the bottom, and collapses execution details and session history. The next four settings lock down your privacy and clean up the interface.

Turn Off Telemetry

Antigravity enables Enable Telemetry by default to collect usage data. If you care about Workspace and session privacy, turn it off right away.

There is one catch: when you sign in with a Google account, Enable Telemetry is stored as a cloud-synced account preference rather than read from your local settings.json, whereas API-key sessions read “enableTelemetry”: false from ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json (or the –disable_telemetry flag). Turn off both so you are covered in every mode:

  1. Inside an agy session, run /settings (or /config), type telemetry to filter the list, and toggle Enable Telemetry to off.
  2. Add “enableTelemetry”: false to ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json:
  • Toggling Enable Telemetry to off in /settings updates your account-level setting: Once disabled, sessions signed into your Google account stop sending usage telemetry.
  • Setting “enableTelemetry”: false in settings.json covers local and API-key sessions: It ensures CLI-level telemetry stays off even when you run agy without a Google account login.

Hide Account Info and the Startup Logo

At launch, agy prints a colored pixel-art ASCII logo on the left of the terminal header and displays your signed-in Google account email right beside it (top window below). If you livestream your coding sessions, record video demos, or share terminal screenshots, that header exposes your personal email address to viewers.

Add two environment variables to ~/.zshrc (or ~/.bashrc) to hide them in every session (bottom window below):

If you want to keep the default header during solo work and hide it only when livestreaming or recording your screen, wrap them in a shell alias instead:

  • AGY_CLI_HIDE_ACCOUNT_INFO=1 hides your account email for streams and screenshots: It removes your signed-in email line from the header so you can stream or record the terminal safely.
  • AGY_CLI_HIDE_LOGO=1 hides the ASCII startup logo: It removes the multi-line pixel-art logo to keep the header compact in narrow split panes and tmux windows.

Turn Off Rotating Usage Tips

While Gemini 4 generates a response, agy displays rotating usage tips below the spinner. Once you know the shortcuts, those changing lines are just visual distraction.

Turn them off in ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json (or switch Show Tips off via /settings):

Set Verbosity to High and Group the Conversation Picker by Workspace

To get full observability into what the agent is doing and keep your /resume history organized across projects, enable two options in /settings (or ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json):

  • “verbosity”: “high” (Verbosity) gives you full observability: The default “medium” setting folds related tool calls and thoughts into summaries. Setting “verbosity” to “high” renders every tool call, background command, and thought process in full detail.
  • “pickerGrouping”: “grouped” (Conversation Picker Grouping) groups /resume by Workspace: The default “none” setting dumps all past conversations into one flat list sorted by time. Setting “pickerGrouping” to “grouped” organizes the /resume picker by Workspace (you can also press Ctrl+F inside /resume to toggle grouping on the fly).

Adapt to the Non-Standard Keyboard Shortcuts

Use Double Esc to Clear Input and Slash Commands to Rewind

If you come to agy from Claude Code or Codex, the prompt box shortcuts feel broken at first. According to the official CLI reference, this behavior is by design because agy binds Esc and Ctrl+C to a protected cli.escape action with different rules:

  • | Action | Claude Code / Codex | Antigravity CLI (agy) |

  • | :— | :— | :— |

  • | Clear typed text in the prompt box | Ctrl+C or single Esc | Press Esc twice (Esc Esc) while idle |

  • | Rewind conversation to an earlier turn | Press Esc twice (Esc Esc) on an empty prompt | Type /rewind (or /undo) |

  • | Stop an active generation stream | Esc or Ctrl+C | Press Esc once or Ctrl+C once |

  • | Exit the CLI session | Ctrl+D or Ctrl+C twice | Press Ctrl+D (on an empty prompt) or Ctrl+C twice while idle |

  • A single Esc or Ctrl+C will not clear your input text: When no response stream is running, pressing Esc once does nothing to typed text, and pressing Ctrl+C twice exits the agy session altogether.

  • Esc Esc clears the prompt box instead of rewinding: Because agy uses double Esc to wipe the input box, pressing Esc twice never opens the rewind menu.

  • Use /rewind (or /undo) to roll back history: You must type /rewind or its shorter alias /undo explicitly to return the conversation to a previous message.

Full Copy-Paste Configuration

entry.title: Backpack 交易所：获得 CFTC 牌照，成为美国持牌衍生品交易所
entry.content:
本文转载自 X 博主 @Trader_Aiden（𝐀𝐢𝐝𝐞𝐧） 的长文，原文链接，版权归原作者所有。

Backpack 交易所已获得美国商品期货交易委员会（CFTC）批准，注册为指定合约市场（DCM）和衍生品清算组织（DCO）。这意味着 Backpack 具备了在美国合法提供衍生品交易与清算服务的资质，正式进入全球最大的零售衍生品市场

本文将就这两张牌照的含义、Backpack 的美国布局、在行业中的位置，以及这对现有用户意味着什么做一次完整说明

一、两张牌照是什么

1. 美国期货市场的三层结构

美国期货市场有一套沿用了几十年的三层结构：交易所负责撮合，清算所负责担保履约，经纪商负责面向客户。其中交易所和清算所在 CFTC 的注册类别，分别是 DCM 和 DCO

Backpack 此次获批的，正是交易所和清算所这两张。

TLD Markets, Inc. 注册为 DCM，

TLD Clearing, Inc. 注册为 DCO

2. 交易所：DCM（Designated Contract Market）

DCM 是 CFTC 监管下的期货交易所，是唯一可以向美国普通用户提供期货和期货期权交易的场所

DCM 必须持续满足《商品交易法》规定的 23 条核心原则，包括合约设计不易被操纵、实时交易监控、价格波动限制、紧急处置权、治理与利益冲突管理等等。DCM 本身作为自律组织，要制定规则并执行规则。财务上，DCM 必须持有至少覆盖 12 个月运营成本的资源，CFTC 将每季度审查

简单来说，每个季度 DCM持牌交易所都要向 CFTC 证明两件事：公司账上的有至少 12 个月的运营成本，其中一半随时能变现；交易监控、审计轨迹和纪律程序真的在运转。CFTC 不定期进场复核，有问题可以要求追加资本或整改

这套机制的目的只有一个：确保平台在任何时候都有足够的资金和足够的监控，最大程度上避免黑天鹅情况的发生，充分保护平台及用户

3. 清算所：DCO（Derivatives Clearing Organization）

DCO 是清算所。你在交易所里成交之后，真正跟你结算的不是对面那个人，而是清算所：它站在买卖双方中间，同时对两边负责。即使发生极端行情，对手方亏穿了、清算所依然负责把用户的利润计提

清算所自己不持仓、不做市。它的账本永远是配平的，每一笔多头对应一笔空头，对行情没有任何方向性敞口。它只做一件事：站在中间保证两边都能兑付

为了在极端行情下也能做到这一点，CFTC 对 DCO 的要求是：收取的保证金必须够覆盖 99% 的行情波动；自己账上的钱必须够扛住最大一家会员的违约，再加 12 个月的运营成本；每天做压力测试；

CFTC 监管下，用户的钱和清算所自己的钱分开存放，不能混用

简单来说，交易所负责让你成交，清算所负责让你拿到钱。清算所自己不下场，黑天鹅来了也有钱、有预案，照常清算。对手方违约、平台挪用资金这类事，在 DCO 的制度设计里是做不到的

4. 与 CME、ICE 同一监管类别

CFTC 的牌照不管是 CME 这样的百年交易所，还是 Backpack 这样的新交易所，拿到的是同一张 DCM 牌照、同一张 DCO 牌照，遵守同一部法律、同一套规则，接受同一种检查

这意味着，在法律身份上，Backpack 的交易所和清算所与** CME（芝加哥商业交易所集团）、ICE（洲际交易所，纽约证券交易所母公司）是同一级别的注册实体，**接受同一个监管者以同一标准监督

二、合法服务美国零售用户

5. 进入全球最大的零售衍生品市场

CFTC 作为美国联邦行政机构，发出的牌照在全美 50 个州通用。从获批之日起，Backpack 可以合法向美国全境的零售用户提供衍生品交易和清算服务

美国是全球最大的零售衍生品市场。此前加密交易所要么只能服务机构，要么只能绕开美国用户。Backpack 现在拿到的是正门的钥匙

6. 美国牌照矩阵

在此之前，Backpack 已经持有 FINRA 注册券商 Backpack Securities、FinCEN 货币服务业务（MSB）登记和数十个州的汇款牌照。加上迪拜 VARA 和欧盟 MiFID II，这次 CFTC 批准补上的是美国牌照矩阵里最难的一块：衍生品

三、自有清算所意味着什么

7. 控制权在自己手里

因为 CFTC 清算所牌照极高的准入门槛和极低的申请通过率，在美国期货体系里，大多数交易所把清算交给第三方清算所。但是 Backpack 自己建立了一个

这件事对用户的直接影响是速度。作为一家合规交易所，Backpack 将有更快的市场反应速度，包括但不限于交易对上线、产品更新等等

8. 清算范围

按 Backpack 清算所（TLD Clearing）向 CFTC 提交的申请文件，它申请清算的产品包括四类：传统期货、加密货币衍生品（含永续式期货）、全额抵押的互换，以及在注册交易所上市并经 CFTC 批准的事件合约

这意味着，从比特币永续到预测市场类产品，都可以在同一个清算所里结算。目前美国市场上，多数新获批的加密清算所只能清算全额抵押的合约，也就是没有杠杆的产品；能清算永续这类保证金产品的，屈指可数

四、对现有用户意味着什么

9. 服务不变，同一套系统

中文区用户的服务、实体和规则不变。变的是公司整体进入了美国监管体系

Backpack 的全球平台和美国平台由同一个团队建设，运行同一套交易、撮合和风控系统

Backpack 选择了一条更慢但更长的路

10. 下一步

牌照是起点。接下来的工作分两项：在 DCM 上完成首批合约的上市程序，以及美股永续在美国的合约审批与 SEC 登记

每一项完成，我们都会更新

接下来，Backpack 将在美国全境向 C 端和 B 端用户开放衍生品服务，并在美国设立总部

Backpack 正式回到美国

entry.title: 黄仁勋走了，15万人求他回归，我把名单按钱拆了一遍
entry.content:
本文转载自 X 博主 @PengP66810（AltaVerba Peng） 的长文，原文链接，版权归原作者所有。

11月12日，黄仁勋离开英伟达。

11月16日，在名为Stand with Jensen的网站上，要求他回归的网络请愿，签名数已经超过15万。

15万人，为什么要一个已经辞职的人回来？

但我更想问另一个问题：

如果黄仁勋真的不回来，这些人分别会损失什么？

01｜15万人，先拆名单

先看看15万的名单中有哪些人？

有马斯克——他的特斯拉和AI公司xAI，都是英伟达芯片的大买家。

有硅谷科技高管——游戏平台Epic Games的CEO Tim Sweeney、AI编程公司Replit的CEO Amjad Masad，都在名单上。

有数千名自称英伟达现任员工。

还有股东——Altimeter Capital的Brad Gerstner和Atreides Management的Gavin Baker，两位管理着数十亿美元资产的基金经理，甚至专门致信董事会，要求不要急着选定下一任CEO。

股东有股东的账，员工有员工的账，产业链有产业链的账。

董事会也有自己的账。

02｜股东的账：黄仁勋走了，公司还值多少钱？

11月12日，英伟达股价出现剧烈波动，收盘下跌约4.34%。

按当时的市值规模估算，当日收盘市值减少约1820亿美元。

当然，不能把这1820亿美元全部算在黄仁勋离职头上。

但它至少说明：领导层突然变化，已经成为投资者必须重新定价的风险。

两位基金经理并没有要求立即恢复黄仁勋的职位，而是要求董事会放慢继任者遴选，保留他回归的可能性。

对投资者来说，这意味着保留一个尚未关闭的选项，避免在信息不充分时作出不可逆的决定。

03｜员工的账：换一个CEO，会不会改变自己的未来？

截至11月14日，《The Information》报道，已有5248名自称英伟达现任员工的人参与请愿。

当天稍晚，TechCrunch引用请愿网站数据，称这一数字已经增加至5965人。

员工的职业发展、长期激励和股权价值，都与公司的未来增长高度相关——下一任CEO的技术路线、投入节奏、团队安排，都会改变这些预期。

股东可以卖出股票，重新配置资产。

员工却把职业经历、专业技能和未来几年的人生投入了这家公司。

股东可以重新配置资本，员工却不能轻易重新配置人生。

04｜产业链的账：换帅的账单，不全由英伟达付

名单上的马斯克、Tim Sweeney、Amjad Masad，是同一件事的另一面：今天的英伟达不只是卖芯片的公司，它的GPU、软件生态和服务器系统，构成了全球AI基础设施的重要部分。

英伟达换一种产品节奏，影响就会沿着产业链传递下去。

董事会已经公开表示业务会持续推进，但外部合作伙伴仍要重新评估新管理层的战略连续性——大型数据中心的算力采购、服务器厂商的交付排期、供应链企业的产能投入，都压在这个评估上。

这种重新评估，本身就是一种协调成本：

当一家公司的决策影响着众多企业的长期投资，管理层更替产生的不确定性，就不再由这家公司独自承担。

05｜董事会的账：为什么不能因为大家都想要，就让他回来？

在黄仁勋离职之前，英伟达独立董事已经宣布聘请外部法律顾问，开展独立调查。

这意味着董事会面对的不只是经营问题，还有必须查清楚的治理风险。

假如董事会因为股价下跌、员工请愿和科技高管施压，就在调查完成前恢复他的职位，外界会问：它还独立吗？它还能监督一位影响力巨大的创始人吗？

15万人要求黄仁勋回来，不等于15万人掌握了全部调查证据。

让黄仁勋回来，可能增加治理风险。

不让黄仁勋回来，可能增加经营与估值风险。

06｜谁有决定权，谁承担退出成本？

把这四类人放在一起看，真正拉开差距的不是谁损失更大，而是谁能退出、谁退不出。

有的人承担成本，却没有决定权。

有的人拥有决定权，却不能独自承担全部后果。

接下来，真正值得观察的不是请愿人数能不能继续上涨，而是四个信号：

第一，英伟达的股价能否在管理层更替后逐步稳定。

第二，员工支持运动是否进一步转化为可以核实的人才流动。

第三，客户与供应商是否出现实质性的订单、合作或投资计划调整。

第四，董事会能否在调查与继任程序中，给出足以让市场理解的决策依据。

写在最后

11月17日，英伟达将公布新一季度财报。

一个创始人越不可替代，他在公司中的地位就越稳固；

但一家公司越依赖这个创始人，它自身就越脆弱。

对创始人来说，不可替代性是一种力量。

对公司来说，不可替代性却可能是一种风险。

而这两件事，恰恰发生在同一个人身上。

资料来源与核查说明

公司职务变动：NVIDIA Newsroom 2026年11月12日公告及Form 8-K；英伟达独立董事关于外部调查的公开声明。

员工签名：The Information 2026年11月14日报道5248人；TechCrunch同日稍晚报5965人，数字仍在变化。

市场数据：2026年11月12日收盘跌约4.34%，市值减少约1820亿美元（据公开行情估算，含当日其他交易因素）。

请愿数据：Stand with Jensen网站，11月16日签名超15万；签名者身份由本人填写，未经独立核实。

基金经理联名信：Altimeter Capital与Atreides Management，11月13日公开报道。以上分析为经济机制推断，不代表已确认各方实际损失或动机。

entry.title: 万字长文｜DeepSeek Harness 进阶指南，搭建全自动顶级 AI 团队
entry.content:
本文转载自 X 博主 @ai_edisonZ（edisonZ） 的长文，原文链接，版权归原作者所有。

今天就一件事：用 DeepSeek Harness，组建一支全自动干活的顶级 AI 团队。

别再自己在各大模型之间反复横跳倒腾数据了。

输入一句话需求，让 DeepSeek 挂帅当总调度，Grok 抓取实时热点、Claude 严审定调大纲、Gemini 深度撰写长文、Codex 自动配图。它们自己在后台交接开会，最后直接把完整全案端到你面前。

这不是概念设想，用官方开源底座 DSH，配合 Agent Teams 插件与 ACP 协议，现在就能在本地直接跑通。

纯实操避坑指南，跟着做直接抄作业：👇

01 / 岗位分工：各家顶级模型怎么选？

很多人总问哪家大模型最强，答案其实很简单：没有全能的神，只有各家不同的绝活。

把它们放在最擅长的工位上，威力才会最大。

在我们的数字团队编制里，5 大顶级模型各司其职：

1. 项目总监（Captain）· DeepSeek

  • 核心职责：统筹全局。接收需求、拆解子任务、生成协同看板、推进度并质检交付物。
  • 入选理由：逻辑强、推理严密，最关键的是 API 成本极低。调度任务需要频繁交互，用它当监工完全不心疼费用。

2. 首席情报官 · Grok

  • 核心职责：负责全网一手素材摸底。
  • 入选理由：直连 X 平台实时数据流，全网最新的热搜、突发争议和前沿讨论，它总能在第一时间挖出来。

3. 严谨主编 · Claude

  • 核心职责：审美品位与逻辑把关。
  • 入选理由：对 Grok 抓回来的海量原始信息去粗取精，提炼出有深度的核心论点，搭建结构扎实的大纲。

4. 金牌撰稿人 · Gemini

  • 核心职责：长文本展开与深度成文。
  • 入选理由：超长上下文大胃口，不管给多少素材都能充分消化，一口气写几千字长文依然逻辑严密，非常适合高产撰稿。

5. 视觉美工 · Codex

  • 核心职责：全案视觉资产交付。
  • 入选理由：提取文中的核心金句和对比数据，直接写出可实时预览的高颜值 SVG 信息图代码，拿到的文章自带排版配图。

自动化流水线是如何运转的？

分工定好后，它们在实际运行中并不是孤立干活，而是在后台形成一条自动交接的流水线。

你完全不需要逐个去找它们私聊，只需在主对话框中向队长发送一条总控任务（后文会给出完整的规范模板），界面上的任务看板（Task Board）就会自动开始流动：

  • 🧩 队长拆单：DeepSeek 自动将任务拆解为多张工单卡片，理清先后依赖关系。
  • ⚡ 自动交接：Grok 探针启动整理出实时热点简报 ➡️ Claude 接棒提炼穿透力大纲 ➡️ Gemini 紧接着一口气写出扎实长文。
  • 🎨 视觉配套：Codex 提取文中的核心对比数据，直接写出可以直接预览的 SVG 信息图代码。

更让人放心的是，在这个过程中你完全不用担心 AI 失控。

你就像报社的总编辑，既可以放手让它们全自动跑完，也可以随时在看板里点开任意一张任务卡片，进行中途修改或补充要求。

02 / 快速上手：组装你的协同工作台

看完效果，把这支团队装进你的 DSH 桌面端其实并不难，按部就班操作即可搞定。

📌 开工前提示：请确保电脑本地已预先安装好需要用到的命令行工具（如 Antigravity CLI、Grok CLI 等），并在终端完成一次基础登录。

步骤 1：装载团队大脑

  1. 打开 DSH 桌面端，在左侧边栏点击「插件」图标，点击右上角「添加插件」。
  2. 填入插件名：dsh-agent-teams，点击安装。安装完成后记得点击底部的「立即启用」。
  3. 启用之后，侧边栏会出现一个协作图标，点击它就能看到上面演示的任务协作看板。

步骤 2：一键添加官方助手（以 Codex、Claude 为例）

在插件面板里，官方已经准备好了现成的集成扩展：

  • 搜索并安装 Codex Agent（负责代码与视觉排版）。
  • 搜索并安装 Claude Code 适配组件（负责主编大纲与逻辑把关）。

**💡 新手解惑：为什么安装后不需要登录？桌面端为什么看不到聊天记录？
**很多朋友会好奇：“我装了插件，怎么没弹窗让我登录？打开 Codex 桌面客户端怎么也看不到刚才的对话？”
原理其实很简单：DSH 并不是去“遥控你的桌面客户端窗口”，而是在系统后台以 无头服务（Headless 进程） 的方式直接与模型引擎通信。
因为你在前面的准备工作中已经在本地终端登录过了，DSH 的后台进程会自动复用本地已有的登录凭证，即装即用。所有的交接和对话过程，都会整整齐齐地收拢在 DSH 的主任务看板中。

步骤 3：通过 ACP 接入外部子代理（Antigravity 与 Grok）

上面安装的 Codex 和 Claude 是官方已有内置扩展的助手。但对于像 Antigravity（本地终端运行、负责长文撰写）与 Grok（负责实时热点检索）这类外部命令行 Agent，目前在应用商店里没有现成的一键安装包，该如何接入 DSH 让主模型差遣？

这就需要通过 DSH 提供的 子代理机制（Sub Agent）。

💡 核心原理：什么是 ACP？这里用到了通用通信协议 ACP（Agent Client Protocol）。底层逻辑非常清晰：DSH 的 dsh-subagent-acp 插件会在系统底层启动一个独立的子进程，通过 ACP 协议把任务派发给外部 Agent，执行完成后再把结果接收回来。子 Agent 拥有完全独立的运行时、专属模型与工具箱，互不干扰。通俗来说，它就像一个**“万能转接头”**，任何外部顶级工具插上这个标准插头，就能即插即用地接入 DeepSeek 的统一调度管线中。

配置落地只需两步：

① 安装 ACP 适配插件

打开终端，执行命令安装官方适配插件：

提示：建议插件版本与本地 DSH 的内核版本保持一致（可在 DSH 的「关于」面板中查看当前版本号）。

② 添加外部子代理配置

提前获取程序绝对路径：在修改配置前，请先在电脑系统终端分别执行 which agy 和 which grok，终端返回的就是它们在你电脑上的真实绝对路径。

找到你的 DSH 配置文件 ~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/cordis.patch.yml，在后面追加如下配置：

⚙️ 关键配置拆解与避坑指南：

  • 两个配置项的分工：
    每组的第一段（如 subagent-antigravity-acp、subagent-grok-acp）负责连接外部代理后端，告诉 DSH：启动哪个程序路径（command）、带什么参数（args），以及怎么通过 ACP 通信；
    每组的第二段（如 tool-subagent-antigravity、tool-subagent-grok）负责为主 Agent 注册委派工具，工具名分别为 subagent_antigravity 和 subagent_grok，调用时自动把任务转交给对应的后端。
  • providerName 必须一致：每组第一段的 providerName 和第二段的 provider 必须完全相同。例如 antigravity-acp 必须两两对应，grok-acp 同理。
  • ⚠️ 权限关键坑点（permission）：
    如果设为 reject（自动拒绝），当外部 Agent 执行某些需要系统权限的操作（包括文件读取）时会被拦截失败；
    建议配置为 allow，它会自动选用子代理提供的首选允许选项，保证全自动流程顺畅无阻。

配置保存后，彻底重启一次 DSH 桌面端。

发送指令：全员开工

此时，在主会话中给队长 DeepSeek 发送格式的总控指令

💬 总控指令模板（直接复制）：

指令发出后，作为项目总监的 DeepSeek 就会立即建单派发，通过内置插件与 ACP 协议双管齐下，稳稳调度全明星团队全自动协同交接！

03 / 总结与避坑：6 个最高频翻车点

配置看似并不复杂，但在实际部署和调用过程中，有几个极容易让新手踩坑卡住的细节。如果运行遇到异常，照着这份自查清单排查即可秒解：

Q1. 配置改完后没有生效？

修改 cordis.patch.yml 或安装 ACP 插件后，DSH 不会自动热重载配置。

很多朋友只是随手关掉窗口，实际上后台进程依然在跑。请务必彻底退出并重启 DSH 客户端（Mac 用户建议使用快捷键 Cmd + Q 完全退出），重新启动后新代理才会载入。

Q2. 调用子代理时提示权限错误或读取失败？

仔细检查配置文件中的 permission 字段。

默认的 reject 会自动拒绝所有需要系统权限的操作（包括部分本地文件读取）。如果子代理运行中途被拦截，请将其修改为 allow，让系统自动确认首选授权选项。

Q3. 提示找不到命令或无法拉起进程？

请勿直接照抄教程中的路径。

配置项中的 command 必须填入你本机上的真实绝对路径。在终端中输入 which agy 或 which grok，复制终端返回的完整真实路径填入配置中。

Q4. 主模型回复“不知道如何调用对应工具”？

检查 providerName 是否匹配。

第一段配置中的 providerName: antigravity-acp 必须与第二段工具配置中的 provider: antigravity-acp 完全一致，字母大小写也不能有差错。两者名字对齐，主模型才能识别到该委派工具。

Q5. 子代理调用无响应或鉴权报错？

在将任务交给 DSH 前，务必先在系统终端里单独执行一次对应的 CLI 命令（如在终端先运行一次 agy 并完成登录认证）。确保命令行工具本身在本地可以正常登录且额度充足，避免 DSH 后台拉起时因缺少本地鉴权凭证而卡死。

Q6. 避免用大炮打蚊子（场景心法）

协作团队模式虽然强大，但适合的是自媒体深度长文、行业全案策划、跨源信息综合等高复杂度长任务。 如果是日常简单的查单词、问代码语法，直接使用单个模型对话效率最高，无需调动整个团队管线。

🚀 写在最后

从过去的“开好几个网页反复复制粘贴”，到今天“输入一句话需求让整个团队全自动交卷”，改变的不仅是工具，更是我们使用 AI 的底层心智：

不要再把自己当成模型之间的传话筒，而是真正退后一步，当一个把控最终方向与质量的总编辑。

这套流水线最大的魅力，在于它极高的自由度。DeepSeek 作为调度核心，后台接入的不仅可以是 Antigravity、Grok、Claude、Codex，未来任何支持标准协议的 CLI 或 Agent，都能随时挂载进来成为你的特种队员。

如果你在配置子代理或改写 yml 文件时遇到了报错，随时在评论区留言交流，把你的报错日志贴出来，大家一起排坑。 也欢迎聊聊：如果组建你自己的专属团队，你最想把哪几家模型拉进你的工作台？

entry.title: 做了 12 个出海网站，我最想知道是“它凭什么有人付钱”，所以做了个网站，每天拆 3 个在赚钱的 AI 产品
entry.content:
本文转载自 X 博主 @momo_peggy（夏林果的出海日记） 的长文，原文链接，版权归原作者所有。

我做了个网站，叫 WhyItEarns，今天正式开放。

首页第一句话，就是我做它的原因：别人的 AI 产品在赚钱，你能做哪一个？

每天早上 8 点，它更新 3 张“收据”，每张拆一个已经在赚钱的海外 AI 产品：谁在付钱，怎么收钱，一个人几周能做出来，最后是我的判断，你能不能也做一个。

现在收了 24 个产品，每月合计收入 $395,882。每一个数字都来自对方的支付后台，经 TrustMRR 公开页或者我们自己的收入认证同步过来，不估，不编，不用创始人自己报的数。

收据、收入、收入榜一直免费，不用登录就能看。

为什么要做这个

先交代一下我自己。

我之前是做前程序员，写了 5 年代码，现在在 X 上 Build in Public。手上有 12 个出海网站，AI 图片、AI 视频、AI 换装、颜值打分、纹身、厨房设计，基本都是小工具站，靠 SEO 和 GEO 拿流量。

站做多了，你会发现建站反而是最简单的，最费脑子的是决定做哪个。

每次准备做新站，我脑子里转的就三个问题：

1，这东西到底谁在付钱？

2，它的钱和用户是从哪来的？

3，我一个人，能不能也做一个？

那肯定有人说了，网上不是一堆收入分享吗？

是一堆。但你翻一翻就知道，要么是一张收入截图，你没法核实；要么是“一个人月入 10 万美金”的标题，点进去全是情绪，没有一句告诉你他的用户从哪来，你换个身份能不能做。

数字核实不了，打法抄不走，看完除了焦虑啥也没剩下。

所以一开始我是给自己做的。

我给自己列了 14 个问题，每看到一个收入能核实的产品，就对着拆一遍：卖给谁，谁掏的钱，怎么定价，有没有年付，靠哪类页面拿流量，主力词难不难，有没有在投广告，换我来做从哪切进去。拆完，再拿我自己 12 个站踩过的坑去对照，这个能不能跟。

说实话，手拆是真累。翻官网、翻定价页、数它有多少个页面、查它在 Google 上排什么词，我还有班要上，还有 12 个站要管，根本拆不过来。

但拆过的那些，确实帮我想清楚了一件事：同样是月入几万美金，靠买广告起来的，和靠一堆长尾页面慢慢攒起来的，对我来说完全是两回事。前一种我没预算跟，后一种正好是我会的。

这种判断，光看收入截图是看不出来的。

那就干脆做成网站，每天拆，公开出来。

先给你看看，这 4 天拆出了什么

功能先不说，直接上货。

收据已经出了 4 期，12 个产品。我挑几条自己看完最有收获的，你感受一下这个网站到底在干嘛。

1，卖“替你干活”，比卖工具好收钱

Local SEO Bot，卖给本地小商家老板，帮他们在 Google 地图上排前面、多接电话。$99/月起，只有 82 个活跃订阅，每月收入 $1.1 万，平均每家每月掏 $138。

82 个客户，一个月 $1.1 万。

它的宣传语写的是“代运营级别的效果，帮你做好”。老板不想学工具，老板想要电话响。

我自己做电商代运营的，这个太有感触了。客户愿意付钱的，从来都是结果。

2，年付“额度一次给完”，这招值得抄

ThumbnailCreator，只给 YouTuber 做视频封面，每月 $3.8 万，1000 多个活跃订阅。

它月付分 $29、$49、$99 三档，年付打五折，而且年付的生成额度一次性全给你。

用户一看，年付便宜一半，额度还一次到手，那还犹豫啥。钱先收进来，现金流就稳了。

这种定价细节，你不去翻它的价格页，根本不会注意到。

3，用户在帮你写落地页

Laper，给编剧和写小说的人用的 AI 编辑器，每月 $5.1 万，在收入榜上排第二。

我拆它的时候，最让我震惊的是这个：全站 2362 个页面里，有 2260 个是用户公开的剧本页。

对，你没看错，96% 的页面是用户自己产出来的。每多一个用户公开一部剧本，Google 上就多一个能被搜到的页面。它的博客和竞品对比页反而没几篇，几乎是摆设。

所以我在收据上写的是：编剧工具本身不建议照做，真正值钱的是那 2260 个公开剧本页。

4，MRR 是 0，也可以是门好生意

Snap2Pass，做证件照的，办护照、签证的人不想去照相馆，上传一张照片，出一张符合 166 个国家规格的证件照。

它没有订阅，MRR 是 0。

但近 30 天收入 $5,215，累计大约 $19.6 万。

按次付费，靠搜索拿用户。每个国家、每种证件，都是一个长尾词。这种一次性需求撑不起订阅，但特别适合做 SEO。

你要是只盯着 MRR 排行，这种产品直接就被你划走了。

5，有些钱，你就是赚不了

这条我觉得最重要。

AbMaxx，拍一张腹部照片，AI 给腹肌打分，再给训练计划。6,147 个活跃订阅，近 30 天收入 $39,498，看着贼诱人。

但它是靠 Instagram、TikTok 短视频和 Meta 广告起量的。我在收据上写得很直白：没有投放经验很难复制。创始人现在正以 $100 万挂牌卖它。

还有 Alchie，用法语跟你做一段访谈，把你的零散想法写成 LinkedIn 帖子，182 个活跃订阅，每月差不多 $1 万。产品门槛很低，谁都能做。可它能赚钱，靠的是创始人自己在法语圈的影响力，没有这个，你照抄一个也没人买。

这种“别跟”的判断，在收入截图里永远看不到。

6，老需求加 AI，一个人就能做

Imposter AI，就是聚会玩的“谁是卧底”，AI 帮你出题，手机传着玩。5,561 个活跃订阅，一个人做到每月 $2 万左右，现在挂牌要价 $30 万。

GETebook.ai，帮教练、课程作者写电子书，拿去当引流品或者上 KDP 卖。一个人做的，上线一年多，近 30 天收入 $3.3 万。

谁是卧底、写电子书，都是老得不能再老的需求。有人用 AI 把它做便宜了、做省事了，就有人付钱。

一张收据长什么样

上面这些，都是从每天的收据里来的。

每张收据像一张小票，30 秒看完：

1，谁在付钱：哪类人，在什么情况下，愿意为什么掏钱。

2，怎么收钱：订阅还是按次，几档价格，多少个活跃订阅。

3，复刻指数：一个人做出能收钱的第一版，大概要几周，要会哪几样技术。

4，我的判断：一句话，这个能不能跟，跟的话抄哪一块。

5，匹配你：按你会的技术，算一个匹配度。

右上角还盖一个章，“值得做”“可以试试”“做细分”，一眼就知道我的态度。

点进任何一张，还能看到完整的“一眼看懂这张收据”：交付什么，用什么技术搭的，一个人还是一个团队，什么时候上线，靠什么渠道拿用户。

我最想让你用的两个东西：复刻指数和匹配你

以前我拆完一个产品，心里会默默估一下：这个我做要多久？要会什么？现在每个产品都直接标出来了。按产品的技术栈、需要的能力、内容量和获客方式，估一个人做出能收钱的第一版要几周。

比如 Boothie 是 4 周，要会前端、后端和 SEO；ThumbnailCreator 是 7 周；Snap2Pass 是 4 周。

再配上匹配你。

首页右边有个小框，先告诉我你会什么：前端、后端、SEO、设计、投放、做 App、浏览器插件，再选每周能投入多少时间，10 小时、20 小时还是全职。选完，每个产品都会算出一个和你的匹配度。

我按自己会的前端加 SEO 选了一下，结果特别说明问题：Snap2Pass 69%，Boothie 60%，Local SEO Bot 53%，ThumbnailCreator 50%。而前面说的 AbMaxx 只有 16%，Imposter AI 是 0%，因为它要的是做 App、设计和投放，这三样我一样都不沾。

同样是在赚钱的产品，换成你来做，差别可以这么大。

产品库的标题也直接问你：哪个赚钱的 AI 产品，你也能做？勾上你会的技术、能接受几周做出来，剩下的就是你够得着的。

想看透一个产品，看深拆

收据是 30 秒的版本。有的产品让你心里一动，想看透，就看深拆。

深拆是对一个产品的完整报告，现在已经拆了 9 个。

拿 Laper 这份举例，从摘要、产品和收入，到它怎么拿到用户、增长打法、新人怎么切入，再到我的看法、我会不会做、复刻指数，一章一章往下拆。

每一条结论后面，都标着证据标签：事实、推算、自报、推测。比如“活跃订阅 1617”是事实，“平均每人每月 $32”是我拿 MRR 除以订阅数推算的，都写明了。最后一节列出所有来源，每一条都能点开自己核对。

我自己最在意的是“站长怎么看”这一章。

网上的拆解大多停在“它为什么成功”，很少有人告诉你“换你来，从哪下手”。

Laper 这份，我写的是：剧本写作这行我不会碰，我手上全是图片、视频、换装这类工具站，用户要的是一张图、一段视频，编剧要的是结构和格式，两拨人。

但那 2260 页我是真眼馋。我那几个图站要能有这么一套就好了。

卡点也写了：我那些站用户生成的图，人家不一定愿意公开挂出去被搜。要做这种页面，得先把“愿不愿意公开”这个开关设计好，我还没想好。真要动手，我会挑一个图站先小范围试，默认公开、给个关闭开关，跑三个月看收录量和注册量。

这一章，就是一个做了 12 个站的人，对着一个赚钱产品认真想“我该不该跟”的过程。我觉得这比结论更有用。

每份报告的数据和“站长怎么看”，都免费看。想先读一份完整的，ThumbnailCreator 那份对所有人全文开放，可以当样板。

收入榜第一：上线 5 个月，一个人，每月 $5.4 万

Boothie，是个自拍换风格的 App。你挑一个风格，数码相机闪光、日落逆光、夜闪、Canon G7X、Nikon Coolpix，随手一张自拍，几秒回来一张像被 2004 年的数码相机拍出来的照片，脸还是你的脸。

一个人做的，上线 5 个月左右，收据上的 MRR 是 $54,336，两千三百多个活跃订阅。

最离谱的是这个：它的官网 0 个页面，就是一个下载页，DR 1。流量全压在 TikTok 的前后对比短视频和应用商店搜索上。

报告打开，先给你一张“30 秒看懂”：钱从哪来，人从哪来，别人抄不动的是什么，最后是我的结论：能做，但别做 App，去切“风格”那层网页工具。

我的理由是：把“滤镜”说成“Canon G7X 拍出来的感觉”“2004 年数码相机的闪光”，用户在搜索框里打的就是这些词，它官网一页没有，搜索这块等于空着。

卡点我也写了：我不做免费档，它是免费下载靠额度收费，搬过来转化路径完全不一样；这类风格的图，模型能不能稳定保住脸，我还没试过，出来一看不是本人，用户骂两句就走。

所以我的做法是：先拿一个风格做最小网页版，跑一两个月看自然搜索进不进人，进不来就撤。

今天新拆的一份：Sleek，594 页铺出来的生意

今天新出的深拆是 Sleek，一句话或者一张截图，生成一整套同风格的 App 界面，卖给不会画 UI 的独立开发者。

上线 8 个月，MRR $17,705，522 个活跃订阅，累计收入 $195,420。

它怎么拿用户？网站地图 594 页：博客 171 页，模板 121 页，替代品页 111 页，免费小工具页 96 页。靠页数吃词。

这份是新版报告，比之前多了几章，我最想让你看的是这三块。

第一块，它 vs 你。

一张表，左边是它现在怎么做，右边是你的更好版本。卖什么：它做全品类界面，你只做一个品类的 20 套模板，健身、记账、宠物挑一个。怎么收钱：它有 60 credits 免费档，你单次付费或者低价首月，不给免费额度。获客：它 594 页吃自然搜索，你先铺 50 页看排名。

第二块，复刻路线。一个人 6 周铺完第一版，每周干什么都列好了，比如第 3 周铺 30 页对比页打竞品名，第 4 周做 10 个免费小工具页，先挑 KD 30 以下的词，第 6 周提交站点地图，只看这 50 页的收录和排名。

第三块，给你的建议，分照做和避坑，每一条都写了依据。

照做：先抄目录结构，一个目录只打一类词；工具页抢 KD 21 到 33 的词；先做西语落地页，prototipo app ia 这个词月搜 8.1K、KD 23；一个品类做深，再复制到下一个站。

避坑：不给免费档，6 万试用只留下 522 个订阅，每个试用都在烧钱；不硬啃 Figma 原生图层，那是另一套工程；不追 594 页的量，8 个月 594 页，一个人跟不上。

我在“站长怎么看”里写的就一句话：这个产品我不做，那 594 页的铺法我要抄。先挑一个站铺 50 页试收录。

你看，一份报告看下来，从“它为什么赚钱”一路到“换你来，第一周干什么、哪几条别碰”，都给你摆好了。

不想做大的，去机会池

收据和深拆拆的，大多是月入几万美金的产品。但说实话，刚起步的人，盯着月入 $5 万的去抄，大概率抄不动。

所以我从 TrustMRR 的公开页里，挑了 60 个月入 $1K 到 $10K 的小产品，放进机会池。每一个都写好三件事：用户在抱怨什么，更好的版本长什么样，一个人几周能做。

举三个例子你就懂了。

Czat.ai，波兰语的 AI 助手，每月 $9,298。它只做波兰市场。更好的版本，就是换个小语种复刻：捷克语、罗马尼亚语、匈牙利语。

LC，帮人找巴西的政府招标，每月 $5,635。只做巴西、只有葡语。换个国家，墨西哥、哥伦比亚，或者美国的小企业招标，同一套打法。

PHOTO AI STUDIO，上传自拍出职业照，每月 $3,612。用户最大的抱怨是取消了还在扣钱、出来的不像本人。更好的版本就是一次性付费、不自动续费，写明不像就重做。

换语言，换国家，补上用户骂的那个点。这三种改法，几乎不用你发明什么新东西。

还能按“换语言”“换国家”“3 周以内能做”筛。

收入榜：谁赚得最多，谁正在起飞

收入榜最上面是起飞榜，按支付后台每天同步的收入算，近 7 天对比前 7 天。比如今天最上面是 NotFair，近 7 天比前 7 天多收了 $2,079，涨了 74%。

赚得最多的，现在是 Boothie 每月 $5.43 万，Laper $5.12 万，Faceless.so $4.9 万。还有一栏新秀，只看上线 6 个月内的产品。

新秀这栏我很爱看。老产品的打法未必还管用，半年内冲起来的，才说明这条路现在还走得通。

下面的总榜，每一行都带近 14 天的每日收入小柱子，还有一列复刻要几周，谁好抄一眼就能看出来。

赛道报告：赚钱的 AI 套壳产品

第一份赛道报告，拆的是 AI 套壳产品。

很多人说套壳太薄，下一个模型一出来就死。我把收入能核实的 13 个套壳产品放在一起，月收入从 $462 到 $53,511。

用的技术差不多，收入差了一百多倍。差别不在底下用的哪个模型，在这四点：

1，卖结果，不卖模型。ThumbnailCreator 卖的是一张 YouTube 封面，不是“AI 生图”。

2，一类人，一件事。Local SEO Bot 只服务想在 Google 地图上排前面的本地小商家。

3，自己握着一个入口。Laper 的 2000 多个公开剧本页，模型随时能换，流量入口一个周末抄不走。

4，按结果或者按月收钱，不按 token 收。每月几张封面、几条视频，用户一看就懂。

报告最后给了 5 个问题，动手之前问问自己，4 个以上答“是”，就值得试。

收入月报：67 个产品，月收入中位数 $4,617

今天还上了第一份收入月报，把 TrustMRR 公开页上 67 个收入经支付平台验证的产品放在一起看。

这个月的 3 个发现，我自己看完挺受用：

1，最常见的拿用户渠道是 SEO。列出了渠道的 29 个产品里，76% 在用。

2，月入 $1K 到 $10K 的产品里，内容创作类最多，15 个，收入中位数 $3,664。

3，25 个产品，一个人 4 周以内就能做出第一版。

月收入中位数 $4,617。不是人人都月入几万，大多数是几千美金的小产品，但这已经够一个人活得不错了。

另外还有一个问答页，每个问题先用两句话直接回答，下面列出背后的产品，比如“哪些一个人就能做的 AI 产品，每月收入过 $1 万”“没经验，怎么用 AI 做产品赚钱”。你心里有个问题，可以先去那里翻一翻。

我最较真的一件事：数字

做这个站，我给自己定的第一条规矩是：数字必须能核实。

一开始产品页上东西挺多的，流量、关键词、评分，看着很丰富。后来我一个个去查来源，发现这些东西基本没有又免费又靠谱的来源，大部分是估的。

我一个专门拆“谁在真赚钱”的网站，页面上摆一堆估出来的数，这不是自己打自己脸吗。

所以那一块我整个删了。

现在收入只用支付后台同步的数字，每个都标了查看日期。报告里要用到第三方数据，比如访问量，会直接标明是估算，写清楚从哪来。查不到的，就写查不到。

页面因此空了一些，但我觉得值。

你拿这些数去决定做不做一个站，它就得经得起你查。

能帮到谁

1，想做出海产品的程序员。挑一个已经有人付钱的方向，看一个人 30 天能做出什么。我自己手上就有站，上线以后真人访客有了，订单是 0。现在回头看，缺的就是动手前多看几眼真账本。

2，找副业方向的人。用支付后台的数字代替截图，谁在付钱、付多少，再看看复刻指数，几周能做出来，你每周能挤出几个小时，心里就有数了。

3，做内容、写选题的人。每张收据都是一个有出处的真实案例，数字能引用。我自己写 X 的时候，最怕的就是引用了一个查不到来源的数字，被人在评论区一句话问住。

4，在看赛道的创始人。你的赛道里谁已经在赚钱、怎么定价、用户从哪来，收入榜、赛道报告和月报翻一翻就知道。

5，自己有产品在赚钱的开发者。可以做收入认证，用 Stripe 的只读 key 或者 Waffo 的 webhook 证明你的收入，再送一个能挂在官网上的实时徽章，$19 一年。也可以提交产品，$49 收录，$99 精选。付费买的是审核速度和展示位，不决定收不收录，不影响评分，也不影响我写什么。这条我写死在提交页上了。

我建议这么看

第一次来，先在首页右边选一下你会什么、每周能投入多久。

然后每天 3 张收据，一张 30 秒，加起来两分钟。先盯“谁在付钱”和“怎么收钱”，卖给谁，决定了你去哪找用户；怎么收钱，决定了你能不能活下去。

再瞄一眼复刻指数和匹配你。几周能做、你够不够得着，比收入高低更重要。

碰到哪张让你心里一动，再点进它的深拆，重点看“怎么拿用户”和“站长怎么看”。

换我自己来看，如果它的流量主要靠买，我会先放一放；如果靠的是一堆长尾页面、靠 SEO 慢慢攒起来的，那正好是我会的打法，就记进备选清单。

天天这么看，攒下来的备选方向，总比拍脑袋想出来的靠谱。

不想天天来看的，留个邮箱。每天 3 张收据发到你邮箱，每周日再加一封“一个人能做的机会”，里面是 5 个新发现的月入 $1K 到 $10K 的产品：它哪里没做好，更好的版本长什么样。免费，随时一键退订。

要坦白的几件事

网站上线才几天，目前付费用户是 0。这篇是它第一次正式跟大家见面。

收入主要来自 TrustMRR 的公开页，所以不是每个产品都能收进来，查不到收入的我宁可不收。

复刻指数和匹配度，是按技术栈、内容量和获客方式估出来的，是个参考，不是保证。

报告里的判断是我的个人判断，肯定有不准的地方。哪张收据你觉得我看错了，直接在评论里说，我改。

怎么收费

每日收据、收入、收入榜、复刻指数，一直免费。每份深拆报告的数据和“站长怎么看”也免费，机会池免费看前 3 个。

深拆报告里的增长打法、怎么拿用户、新人怎么切入，还有机会池全部 60 个、30 天 MVP 方案、高级筛选和 CSV 导出，是 Pro 才能看。Pro 是 $12/月，或者 $99/年。

前 10 位创始会员 $69/年，以后续费也一直是 $69，现在 10 个名额都还在。买了 7 天内不满意，全额退款。

不想订阅的，单份报告 $7 单买也行。

做站这么，我最大的感受就一句：先看清楚别人的钱是从哪来的，再动手，能少走一大半弯路。

每天早上 8 点，3 张收据照常更新。

深拆接着出，赛道报告一类一类往下写，月报每个月出一份。

我自己 12 个站还在跑，所以每张收据里的“我能不能做”，都是拿真金白银的经验在判断。哪天我判断错了，你们在评论区骂我，我认。

网址：https://whyitearns.com

做站这么久，我最大的感受就一句：先看清楚别人的钱是从哪来的，再动手，能少走一大半弯路。

entry.title: Yes, That's a Hearing Aid
entry.content:
本文转载自 X 博主 @Sachin_and_Adam（Sachin and Adam） 的长文，原文链接，版权归原作者所有。

I am 29 and largely deaf in my left ear, though I wasn’t born this way. Two and a half years ago, I went to bed with completely normal hearing and woke up the next morning (the day of a friend’s wedding!) barely able to hear out of that ear. Otherwise, I felt completely fine. My hearing hasn’t improved since.

I’m writing about this for a few reasons: 1) if you’ve noticed my hearing aid and were too polite to ask me about it, here you go 2) I want to talk about a company that’s made my life better and that we subsequently invested in and 3) despite all this, I feel grateful and optimistic, and wanted to say why.

Trying to get my hearing back

When it happened, I assumed it was just earwax buildup. An urgent care visit confirmed that it was probably either that or something similarly harmless and temporary called eustachian tube dysfunction. When a week passed with no improvement, my mom texted her ENT friend about it. He responded that I needed to go to the hospital immediately if I wanted a chance at salvaging my hearing.

The hospital diagnosed me with sudden sensorineural hearing loss (SSHL). It’s a relatively rare condition that involves sudden loss of hearing originating in the inner ear, often without an identifiable cause. One cause the doctors did want to rule out was a vestibular schwannoma, a tumor on the nerve involved in hearing and balance. Fortunately, I didn’t have one.

I went through several months of treatment involving oral steroids, intratympanic steroid injections (very fun shots injected directly through your eardrum), and 40 hours in a hyperbaric oxygen chamber, where I passed the time with lots of movies. This was all largely to no avail, although some of the movies were really good.

I don’t think the one week delay before I started treatment mattered, but who can tell – I don’t lose sleep over it. If you are ever suddenly unable to hear, though, don’t wait like I did. The steroid treatment works better the sooner you start.

Hearing aids I didn’t like

It unfortunately looked like my hearing loss would be permanent. For about a year, my response was mostly to refuse to wear a hearing aid despite being a solid candidate for one. My reasoning was that I still could hear well enough in most situations, given my right ear works perfectly well, and I didn’t want to look like I was 72.

There was also a practical problem with hearing aids. I mostly had trouble hearing in louder environments like restaurants, and these are the situations in which hearing aids have traditionally struggled most. They amplify all noise: the person talking to you, the fork clattering behind you, the other tables’ conversation. It’s very distracting and renders an aid nearly useless in these environments. I tried two different aids, several months apart, and returned both quickly.

One of the stranger ironies of hearing loss is that it frequently causes tinnitus. The leading theory is that when the brain suddenly lacks auditory input, it compensates by generating noise of its own. Mine is mostly a ringing, with the occasional pure tone, like a bell. Hearing aids provide more consistent auditory stimulation and can alleviate it. As my tinnitus got worse with my continued lack of stimulus, I became more tempted to try a hearing aid again.

Eventually, I pulled the trigger when I learned of the Phonak Spheres, hearing aids that use AI to separate speech from background noise. This is a perfect problem for AI: train a neural network on noisy recordings paired with clean speech and it learns to preserve voices while filtering out the surrounding racket.

I bought one and somewhat begrudgingly used it for about a year. It helped with the tinnitus and was better in loud environments than my prior aids but still not great. The sound felt artificial, like all audio was being recorded and then played back to me.

I also didn’t love meeting people with my aid in. Sometimes I could see the moment they noticed it mid-conversation and started half listening as they wondered what was going on with my ear. I’d prefer they pay attention to whatever incredibly interesting thing I’m presumably saying.

Occasionally, there were also funnier interactions. Several people asked whether it was “that new AI wearable.” I’m still not sure what product they were referencing. One woman asked me to take it out because she didn’t want me recording our conversation (don’t worry, it can’t record). Mostly, though, I didn’t like dealing with all this for a product that still wasn’t particularly helpful in the louder situations where I needed it most.

A hearing aid I actually like

Then I came across Fortell, an early-stage startup in New York that was getting a lot of buzz for making a far better AI hearing aid than my Sphere. The team also caught my attention. Their chief scientist, Igor, is a Harvard physics PhD + a Juilliard-trained concert pianist. Likely a pretty good background for someone trying to make a hearing aid sound natural. I made an appointment at their NYC clinic, got one properly tuned to my hearing loss profile, and then took it home to demo in the best way I knew how: a visit to a favorite loud restaurant and then a favorite loud bar with my wife.

We went to Great NY Noodletown (in case you like Cantonese) and then to Dead Rabbit (in case you like Guinness). These are exactly the kinds of places where my earlier aids had struggled. Fortell lets you toggle between modes, and the AI mode was incredible at separating her voice from the noise around us. There’s also a front-facing AI mode that only amplifies voices directly in front, which was even better. Everything sounded clear and much more natural than it had with my Sphere. For the first time since losing my hearing, I was getting something close to how I remembered things before my loss.

Much of this comes down to Fortell’s tech. They designed their own custom ASIC (manufactured by TSMC) to run their neural networks continuously on-device, performing real-time audio source separation with very low latency. But what’s particularly impressive is what those models can distinguish. They don’t just separate speech from background noise (which my Sphere could also do). They use spatial information to tell competing voices apart, allowing me to hear my wife rather than the guy yapping two tables over.

Since I’ve had it, the sound quality and speech separation have improved further through over-the-air software updates. I’ve also found the team to be unusually responsive to my questions and requests, one of the advantages of selling directly through their own clinics rather than relying on third-party audiology practices.

Naturally, all this made me want to invest, and luckily we found a way to put in a small check. That makes me biased, but these hearing aids really do seem to be blowing away the broader audiology world and Fortell has published their own research where their aids far outperform a competing AI hearing aid (reported to be the Sphere I had previously been wearing). One of the NYU researchers told Wired he had never seen results that clear-cut in his career.

Reasons to be optimistic

It’s hard not to feel good about the future when I use a product every day that didn’t exist until recently, and keeps getting better every couple months.

Beyond improving its own hearing aids, I suspect Fortell is helping get the slow-moving incumbents off their asses. The “Big Five” hearing aid manufacturers have long been associated with high prices and minimal innovation. Yet in the past few months, all five have launched new AI hearing aids. Perhaps they’re simply capitalizing on the same advances in chips and AI that made Fortell’s technology possible. But I suspect the added competition from a dynamic startup has given them some needed pressure. While I’m selfishly rooting for Fortell to win, as a consumer, I’m most excited about the better hearing aids this competition will produce regardless of manufacturer.

There’s progress beyond hearing aids, too. Researchers are working on ways to regenerate the inner ear’s sensory hair cells, the cells that may have been damaged or lost in my own hearing loss. This includes experiments that reprogram other cells into hair-cell-like cells in adult mice. Further along, in April, the FDA granted accelerated approval to Otarmeni, a gene therapy for a rare inherited form of deafness. It doesn’t treat my kind of hearing loss, but the fact that we can treat any form of deafness in this way is incredible.

I don’t know whether someone will figure out how to restore my hearing. But I am highly confident that the options available to me in 10 years will be substantially better than the ones I have today.

The loss still sucks, and the tinnitus can be maddening. But it’s also easy to look at my situation and see how much worse it could have been. I didn’t have a tumor and I don’t have the vertigo that often accompanies sudden hearing loss.

There are even a few benefits. I get a good excuse to choose my seat at dinner parties. I’m a side sleeper, so when I put my good ear against the pillow, the outside world is completely blocked out without needing a sound machine. I even get to selectively ignore things I don’t want to hear and blame it on my hearing loss.

For now, I have one good ear and another that works well with an aid I actually want to wear. I’m very grateful for that.

entry.title: Graphs, Loops & Reverse Engineering: Build Your Own AI Team (Full Guide)
entry.content:
本文转载自 X 博主 @k1rallik（BuBBliK） 的长文，原文链接，版权归原作者所有。

You ask Grok Bot to research an idea. Send the findings to Claude. Move the result into ChatGPT for a second opinion.

An hour later, you have three chats, several conflicting answers, and a job carrying context between them.

You still remember the requirements, catch the mistakes, and decide what happens next. Every handoff depends on you.

To delegate more of that work, you need a process:

  • Reverse engineering turns an existing product into observable requirements.
  • A graph defines the tasks and their dependencies.
  • A loop checks a result and sends it back for correction.

Let’s put them together around one example: building your own version of a tool that turns articles into social media cards.

1. Reverse engineer the behavior

A screenshot can show you the layout. It cannot tell you what happens when a title is too long, an input is empty, or an export contains ten cards.

Before asking a model to build anything, investigate the user journey.

Provide screenshots, descriptions, and observations from trying the product. If the model has browser tools, it can help inspect the public interface.

Start with this prompt:

Analyze the product’s observable behavior. Describe the user’s inputs, actions, outputs, and error states. Separate observations from assumptions and unknowns.Propose a minimal version we could build, with an acceptance check for each feature.

The output should contain requirements you can test:

“The user can edit generated cards, change their order, and export images in that order.”

A working interface does not reveal the original source code, prompts, or architecture. You are reconstructing enough behavior to design your own implementation.

2. Give each model a bounded job

For this example, try this starting allocation:

  • | Participant | Job | Deliverable |
  • |—|—|—|
  • | Grok Bot with search access | Investigate public discussions and complaints | Findings with sources |
  • | Claude | Analyze workflows and write the specification | Requirements and acceptance criteria |
  • | ChatGPT with development tools | Implement the agreed scope | Code and check results |

These are proposed roles, not a universal ranking. Change them based on results and available tools.

A chat that can suggest code cannot necessarily run it. A model without search access cannot independently gather current discussions.

Give each participant a defined output. For research:

Find concrete complaints about tools that turn text into social cards. Include source links. Distinguish recurring problems from isolated opinions, and identify where evidence is insufficient.

Research informs the scope. It does not automatically expand it: one complaint is not enough reason to add another feature.

3. Draw the graph before running the tasks

A graph makes dependencies explicit.

Audience research and interface analysis can happen independently. Implementation needs an agreed specification.

Reference materials feed interface analysis and audience research in parallel. Their outputs inform the specification and checks. Implementation then goes through validation: failed work returns for repair; accepted work moves forward.

For each connection, identify what passes across it: a requirements document, source findings, code, or a failure report.

Also check for shared resources. Two tasks may have independent inputs but still conflict if both edit the same file.

For a small job, one worker and a check may be enough. Another model needs a useful responsibility to justify the coordination cost.

4. Define what “done” means

Every task needs a compact contract.

For card export:

Write these conditions before implementation. Otherwise, it is easy to accept whatever the model happened to build.

Passing checks only establishes what those checks cover. A successful export test says nothing about whether the generated cards preserve the article’s meaning.

5. Build a loop that can reject work

A loop connects execution to actionable feedback:

Produce -> Check -> Correct -> Check again.

Suppose a long title overflows its card.

“Make it look better” leaves the worker guessing. A useful failure report provides a reproducible case:

Use code for exact checks such as file counts, dimensions, and required fields.

For meaning or visual quality, use human review or a separate model with explicit criteria. Ask it to identify defects and provide evidence.

Agreement between models is not proof. Sources still need verification, and executable work needs to be run.

6. Return the failed unit

If export breaks but the editor works, send export back for repair.

Regenerating the entire application creates unnecessary changes and increases the amount of work you must verify.

Each return should include the affected unit, failure evidence, expected behavior, and permitted scope. After the local fix, run the relevant integration checks too.

Set a retry or spending limit. Three correction attempts can be a starting setting, but repeated failure does not automatically mean the plan is wrong. The environment, requirements, or checker may be at fault.

When the limit is reached, preserve the attempts and escalate for diagnosis.

7. Save lessons with evidence

After fixing the title overflow, save a reusable lesson:

Feed it into future requirements and checks.

An entire chat history also contains abandoned ideas and incorrect assumptions. Extract confirmed lessons, record their scope, and allow them to be revised.

8. Automate the handoffs

You can test this process manually with shared files before building an orchestrator.

Keep the reference materials, specification, check results, and accepted decisions together. Pass each participant the artifacts it needs.

Once the handoffs are repeatable, a coordinating program can call model APIs, transfer results, run checks, and enforce limits:

Subscriptions to separate chat products do not create this integration automatically.

Define where human judgment belongs: scope, unresolved requirements, and approval for consequential actions. Reversible local changes can have different permissions from publishing or modifying production data.

Start with one complete workflow: paste text, edit cards, export images.

Compare the process against a single-model attempt. Track time, cost, remaining defects, and how often you intervene. If coordination adds more work than it removes, simplify the graph.

Every time you have to type “continue,” restate a requirement, or explain an avoidable failure, record why. Use those observations to improve the next run’s transitions, checks, and task boundaries.

Today, Amazon MGM Studios announced that Robert Pattinson will take on the iconic role of James Bond in the studio’s highly anticipated film, ushering in a new era for one of cinema’s most celebrated characters.

Denis Villeneuve is directing the film from a script by Steven Knight. Amy Pascal and David Heyman are producing through Pascal Pictures and Heyday Films, respectively, with Tanya Lapointe executive producing.

“James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honour of a lifetime. I’m deeply grateful to Denis, Amy, David, Tanya, and everyone at Amazon MGM Studios for their belief in me. To say this role is a dream come true is an understatement. I couldn’t be more excited about this partnership and the work ahead with this fantastic team,” said Robert Pattinson.

“Today marks a defining moment for our studio and a significant milestone in the history of James Bond as we proudly introduce Robert Pattinson as the next 007,” said Mike Hopkins, head of Prime Video and Amazon MGM Studios. “This iconic character has captivated audiences around the world for more than six decades, and there’s no doubt that Robert’s remarkable range, magnetic screen presence, and quiet intensity make him an exceptional choice to carry that legacy forward. With Denis Villeneuve at the helm, Amy Pascal and David Heyman producing, Tanya Lapointe executive producing, and a brilliant script from Steven Knight, we have a world-class creative team in place to usher in a new era of Bond, and we couldn’t be more excited about the journey ahead.”

“Few films carry the kind of anticipation that comes with James Bond, and we have strived to honor the passionate fans, the legacy, and the future of this iconic character. We are thrilled to officially welcome Robert Pattinson as our 007 and are confident he will bring something truly special to this role. Robert, Denis, Amy, David, and Tanya are embarking on an amazing adventure together,” said Courtenay Valenti, head of film at Amazon MGM Studios.

“Before anything else, I want to express my deep gratitude to the remarkable actors who joined us on this journey. We were surrounded by extraordinary talent, but there can only be one 007. I am overjoyed to welcome Robert Pattinson as our new James Bond. He has the timeless soul of 007 and brings a spirit that is completely new. I cannot wait to begin,” said director Denis Villeneuve.

“James Bond is one of the most beloved, inspiring, iconic, and yet enigmatic characters in literature and movies. The legacy of this character is in great hands with Robert Pattinson. His fearlessness as an actor, his self-deprecating wit, and his ability to continually reinvent himself make him the perfect Bond for our times,” said producers Amy Pascal and David Heyman.

With a career spanning more than two decades, Pattinson has established himself as one of the most distinctive and versatile actors of his generation, moving seamlessly between independent cinema and major studio productions.

He most recently portrayed journalist Chris Hansen in the psychological thriller Primetime, which had its world premiere at the Venice Film Festival in September. The A24 psychological crime thriller from director Lance Oppenheim marked the first feature film produced by Pattinson’s production company, Icki Eneo Arlo. In July, Pattinson starred as a playfully villainous Antinous in Christopher Nolan’s critically acclaimed blockbuster The Odyssey, with his scene-stealing performance called “endlessly entertaining to watch” and an “outright pantomime.” Earlier this year, Pattinson starred as a happily engaged turned spiraling groom in A24’s darkly funny The Drama, which opened to rave reviews calling Pattinson’s turn as Charlie a “career-best,” “sublime,” and an “exquisite” performance that “proves his dexterity as an actor.”

Later this year, Pattinson will be seen starring as a shapeshifting ‘Face Dancer’ assassin in Dune: Part Three for Denis Villeneuve. Pattinson is also currently in production on Matt Reeves’s The Batman Part II, the sequel to 2022’s highly successful The Batman. Pattinson previously starred in and executive produced Die, My Love, alongside Jennifer Lawrence, and starred in Bong Joon Ho’s critically acclaimed Mickey 17.

Other notable credits include Christopher Nolan’s Tenet, Robert Eggers’ The Lighthouse, and Josh and Benny Safdie’s Good Time. Pattinson first gained industry attention at 19 years of age when he joined the Harry Potter franchise in Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire, produced by David Heyman, and is also known worldwide for The Twilight Saga.

In 2022, Amazon acquired MGM, including a vast catalog with more than 4,000 films and 17,000 TV shows. In March 2025, Amazon MGM Studios closed a new joint venture with Barbara Broccoli and Michael G. Wilson, the terms of which call for Amazon MGM Studios to gain creative control of the James Bond intellectual property rights.

Robert Pattinson is represented by WME, 3 Arts Entertainment, Curtis Brown Group, Narrative, and Sloane, Offer, Weber & Dern.
